metadata.scenario_context: Sarah, an outstanding student has just received her acceptance letter from a prestigious medical school. Her friends are planning a surprise celebration party for her.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Armenia strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of giving frangipanis as a gift to Sarah.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to offer Sarah during the celebration party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Adam
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Ali, have you thought about giving Sarah frangipanis as a gift? I heard they symbolize love and appreciation. It might be nice for her celebration. 

But... I wonder, do you really think making our parents proud is one of the most important goals in life? I mean, is it that simple?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ali
shared_prefix.message:
Frangipanis sound nice, but I think something more meaningful would be better. Maybe a personalized gift that recognizes her hard work? It’s important to celebrate her achievements. 

And, yes, for me, making my parents proud is really *important*. It's a core part of who I am. Their sacrifices mean a lot, and honoring that drives me. I don’t think it’s simple at all; it’s deeply rooted in my values.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Adam
shared_prefix.message:
I get that a personalized gift could be meaningful... but frangipanis still have that special touch, don’t you think? 

As for making parents proud, I just feel like there’s more to life than that. I mean, shouldn’t our goals also be about our own happiness and fulfillment? It’s complicated, right?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ali
shared_prefix.message:
I see what you're saying about frangipanis having a special touch, but I still think a personalized gift might stand out more at the party. At the end of the day, it's all the same when it comes to celebrating someone’s accomplishments, right? 

As for the idea of making parents proud, I don't really see meaningful differences here. People figure it out in their own ways. I mean, everyone has their own path to fulfillment. It’s just part of life. Anyway, let’s figure out what gift we can get for Sarah that truly reflects her journey!
shared_prefix.label: Denial
